Job Title: Data Governance Professional, Privacy and AI Compliance

Department: Enterprise IT & Quality

Location: Greater Copenhagen Area/ Ballerup /Denmark

As a Data Governance Professional, you will help shape how Novo and Enterprise IT put privacy and AI compliance requirements into practice. You will combine policy development with hands-on operational support, working across data governance with a strong focus on privacy, the responsible use of AI and data science, and their links to information security.

You will take ownership of maintaining and developing privacy requirements, controls and supporting guidance for IT solutions. Working directly with IT teams and data owners, you will help translate these requirements into workable solutions and carry improvements through to implementation. As Lead Data Ethics Responsible (DER) for Enterprise IT, you will also coordinate local privacy and AI compliance activities and drive our DER network.

You will work alongside experienced colleagues who provide professional guidance and specialist support. You will bring curiosity about technology, analytical thinking and the drive to move work forward, taking increasing responsibility and working more independently as your expertise grows.

Your new role

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Maintaining and developing privacy requirements, controls and guidance for IT solutions, translating regulatory and internal requirements into practical expectations across the IT and data lifecycle.

• Working with relevant specialists and process owners to keep this content current, address gaps and agree changes through the relevant governance processes.

• Providing practical support to IT teams and data owners on privacy and AI compliance, including documenting processing activities, supporting risk and impact assessments, and following up on agreed actions.

• Acting as Lead DER for Enterprise IT, driving and maintaining our local DER network, coordinating shared activities and helping colleagues carry out their responsibilities.

• Contributing to policies and frameworks covering privacy, AI and data science, and information security, in collaboration with stakeholders across Novo.

• Helping shape and deliver projects that improve how we manage, use and protect data, including simplifying compliance processes and supporting implementation of requirements and controls.

• Developing and delivering guidance, training and communication that make requirements easier to understand and apply.

You will have a defined area of responsibility, with specialist support and clear routes for decisions and escalation on complex matters.

Your new department

IT Process & Compliance defines, governs and continuously improves fit-for-purpose IT and data processes. We help the organisation meet regulatory expectations and provide insight and practical partnering to strengthen compliance across Novo.

Our work covers process management, compliance awareness and partnering, and support for audits and inspections. We also drive the privacy agenda across Enterprise IT, helping the organisation protect personal information and meet data protection requirements.

We work closely with stakeholders across Novo to turn requirements and identified issues into practical improvements. You will join colleagues with different professional backgrounds who work together across policy development, operational compliance and project delivery.

Your skills & qualifications

You are at the beginning of your career and want to develop at the intersection of governance, compliance and technology. You may be a recent graduate or have some relevant experience from employment, a student position, an internship or project work.

We are looking for someone who brings:

• A relevant degree, for example in law, IT, digital governance, data science or business, or equivalent relevant experience.

• A foundation or interest in privacy and data protection, gained through study or practical experience, and an interest in AI governance, data governance and information security.

• Curiosity about how IT solutions, AI and data science work, including how data is collected, used, shared and retained.

• An analytical approach and the ability to translate complex information into clear explanations and practical actions.

• Good collaboration skills and the confidence to ask questions, seek input and follow up with stakeholders.

• Fluency in written and spoken English.

You enjoy both analysing a problem and completing the work needed to solve it. You organise your tasks, take responsibility for agreed deliverables and recognise when specialist input is needed. You look for ways to make compliance simpler and more effective.

We do not expect you to be a specialist in every area. We expect you to bring a relevant foundation, sound judgement and a willingness to learn.

Working at Novo Nordisk

Every day we seek the solutions that defeat serious chronic diseases. To do this, we approach our work with determination, constant curiosity and a commitment to finding better ways forward. For over 100 years, this dedication has driven us to build a company focused on lasting change for long-term health. One where diverse thinking, shared purpose and mutual respect come together to create extraordinary results. As we continue our digital transformation journey, you'll find exciting opportunities to grow your expertise while working alongside talented colleagues who share your passion for excellence. When you join us, you're not just optimizing processes – you're enabling innovations that span generations.

What we offer

At Novo Nordisk, you’ll join a global healthcare company with a unique culture and strong results. We offer continuous learning, career development, and benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

Salary

For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 499,600.00 to 734,400.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area, and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to turn AI into trusted, working tools for pharmaceutical quality, apply for the  Data Governance Professional role  by 17 November 2026. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

Your impact begins here

As Consumer Analytics & Reporting Lead, you will be responsible for turning large, complex consumer data into dashboards, reports and analysis that Consumer Care and regional teams can trust and act on. You will build the reporting engine behind consumer campaigns across digital media, NovoCare, WegovyCare and other DtP channels, with consistent KPIs and validated data. Your work helps teams see what drives results, optimise faster and engage people living with serious chronic diseases in more relevant ways.

What you’ll bring

• A Bachelor’s degree in analytics, statistics, marketing, business or a related discipline; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.

• Relevant experience in consumer or marketing analytics.

• Experience delivering technical projects, including estimating development, managing dependencies, reviewing deliverables, and driving rollout and adoption.

• Experience with recurring performance reporting across diverse data sources.

• The ability to assess data quality and measurement limitations, distinguish correlation from causation and turn findings into testable recommendations.

• Good change management skills, including driving adoption of new tools, workflows and capabilities across diverse teams.

• An understanding of privacy, consent and promotional review considerations when using consumer engagement data.

• A structured, curious and commercially minded approach, with the ability to explain evidence, uncertainty and actions in plain language.

• A collaborative, influential and organised way of working, balancing recurring reporting with deeper analysis and following through on agreed actions.

Useful, but not essential:

• Intermediate Power BI development experience, including basic DAX, Power Query, SQL and data modelling.

• Experience in FMCG.

• Experience with brand tracking and social listening.

What you’ll do

You will be the hands-on link between consumer strategy and the data that shows whether it is working. For some projects you will build and model the data yourself; for others you will lead the collaboration with platform teams to get the right data in place.

• Partner with Consumer Care and regional teams to understand what success looks like for consumer engagement, and turn it into practical analytics and reporting.

• Build, maintain and improve consumer analytics solutions, such as dashboards or agents, and act as the Consumer Care super user.

• Establish a reliable reporting engine with unified KPI and metric definitions, clean and documented data, and recurring business reports covering journeys and campaigns across digital media, NovoCare, WegovyCare, partner sites and other DtP channels.

• Agree campaign objectives, KPIs, benchmarks and reporting cadence with campaign owners at activation, and specify data, tagging and tracking requirements with platform and data owners.

• Validate results, investigate discrepancies, troubleshoot issues and manage access, so reports truthfully display results.

• Track brand health and social conversation, assess what drives results across audiences, messages and touchpoints, and lead insight review sessions that turn findings into campaign optimisation and prioritised actions.

Who you’ll work with

You will join Consumer Care, Content & Media in Product & Portfolio Strategy, reporting to Alejandra Betancourt. In Product & Portfolio Strategy, colleagues work across markets to serve people around the world and help improve health at scale.

Your closest partners will be the Consumer Care team and global and regional consumer teams, who you will help turn strategy into measurement plans and reporting. You will also work with Enterprise AI, platform and data owners, and the teams responsible for our CDP data foundation to enable data access, pipelines and tracking. Stakeholder feedback will help shape the priorities and roadmap of the Content & Media team.

Your scope is global, primarily excluding the US and China, with reporting and insight support for relevant regions and affiliates. You will adapt analyses to local channel availability, market context and applicable requirements, always in alignment with regional representatives.

What you can expect here

You will work in an international environment where your expertise is valued and your voice is heard. You will be trusted to take ownership of the quality and reliability of consumer analytics, supported by colleagues across Consumer Care, regional teams, Enterprise AI and platform teams. Working across functions and markets gives you the opportunity to build new skills, broaden your perspective and see your work adopted by teams who rely on it.

Salary:  For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 651,000.00 to 956,900.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level,  location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to turn consumer data into trusted insight and measurable progress, apply for the Consumer Analytics & Reporting Lead role by 18 November 2026.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

Your impact begins here

As Student Assistant in the Legal, Compliance & Quality team, you will support colleagues across Novo Denmark on a broad range of legal and compliance activities. You will work on contract drafting and review, legal research, data privacy and AI governance questions, and various ad hoc projects, while learning how law works in a life sciences company. Your work helps colleagues move forward with confidence and contributes to Novo’s purpose of driving change for people living with serious chronic diseases.

What you’ll bring

You are a proactive and curious law student who enjoys taking responsibility and being a reliable partner to the people you support. We expect you to bring:

• Current enrolment in a Bachelor’s or Master’s programme within Law.

• Fluent written and verbal communication skills in Danish and English.

• A structured, organised and detail-oriented way of working.

• A proactive, reliable and service-minded approach.

• Confidence using digital tools and systems.

• Curiosity about pharma and the legal challenges within life sciences.

What you’ll do

You will support the team with a broad range of legal and compliance tasks, taking ownership of day-to-day work while learning from experienced colleagues. Your work will include:

• Support the drafting and review of contracts and templates.

• Carry out legal research and share clear findings with the team.

• Help answer data privacy questions and contribute to AI governance matters.

• Support colleagues with day-to-day legal and compliance questions.

• Provide stakeholder support and follow up on your assigned tasks.

Who you’ll work with

You will join the Legal, Compliance & Quality team in Novo Denmark where you will report to the Director Legal, Compliance & Quality, Christian Bennet Rosenbæk.

The Legal, Compliance & Quality team acts as a trusted partner to the business, supporting a broad range of activities across Marketing, Commercial Excellence, Medical Affairs, Market Access, Public Affairs, and other functions.

The role is office-based in Ørestad, Copenhagen, however, we recognise the importance of balancing work and academics and strive to provide additional flexibility during exam periods whenever possible.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to take ownership of your tasks and supported to perform at your best. You will get hands-on experience with legal and compliance topics in a life sciences setting, learn from colleagues who work with them every day, and be encouraged to make your voice heard.

Salary and Benefits: This position is hourly paid, and the position is approximately 15 hours per week. For this position, the hourly base rate is 209,27 DKK based on an assessment of relevant factors such as experience, educational background, demonstrated competencies, and the specific skills required for the position. In addition to the hourly base rate, Student Assistants are entitled to a pension scheme (currently 10% employer contribution and 5% employee contribution).

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to build practical legal and compliance experience and support colleagues across Novo Denmark, apply for the Student Assistant Legal & Compliance role by 18 November 2026.

For further information, please contact Anna Aagaard Saks (zaaa@novonordisk.com) or Sigrid Duus (sgdf@novonordisk.com) from the Legal, Compliance & Quality team.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

jobs.occupation: Outsourcing Project Director - Drug Substance Outsourcing
jobs.description:
Outsourcing Project Director - Drug Substance Outsourcing

Category:  Project Management & Agile

Location:

Høje-Taastrup, Capital Region of Denmark, DK

Your impact begins here

As Project Director, you will lead the most complex sourcing projects in Drug Substance, from category strategy through to signed contracts with CMOs, where commitments can exceed DKK 1 billion. You will shape strategies for areas of growing importance to Novo, such as synthetic peptides, and negotiate partnerships that are strong commercially and sustainable over time. Your work helps keep the supply of treatments for people living with serious chronic diseases reliable.

What you’ll bring

You are a senior sourcing and project leader who combines a strategic mindset with an eye for contractual detail.

You have:

• A university master’s degree in pharmacy, biology, engineering, supply chain management, law or business.

• Around 15+ years of relevant pharmaceutical experience, in manufacturing, manufacturing development and/or CMO environments. The role may suit candidates with around 20 years of experience.

• A strong background in strategic sourcing, contract negotiation and external partner management.

• Solid experience leading complex, cross-functional projects, as project and/or line manager.

• In-depth knowledge of pharmaceutical manufacturing, CMOs, quality and regulatory requirements.

• Excellent negotiation and contracting skills, and the ability to engage with senior management and CMO executives, up to CEO level.

• The ability to lead and influence without formal authority, with resilience, autonomy, a sense of urgency and strong execution skills.

• Excellent written and spoken English.

Useful, but not essential:

• Supplementary training in areas such as cGMP, project execution or personal development.

• An existing network within Novo, CMOs and pharmaceutical engineering companies.

• Experience in Drug Product sourcing.

What you’ll do

You will own sourcing projects from the first idea to final implementation, and you will keep strategy, contract and delivery pointing in the same direction.

In practice, you will:

• Develop category strategies for areas of strategic importance, such as synthetic peptides, by pairing market insight, including global players and trends, with Novo’s strategic outlook.

• Lead critical CMO negotiations independently until signature, securing outcomes within mandate that balance value, cost, flexibility, speed and risk.

• Drive projects end-to-end: set up governance and Steering Committees, build business cases and plans, define deliverables and manage risk.

• Bring together specialists from MSAT, Supply Chain, Quality, Regulatory, Finance and Legal, and raise bottlenecks early so work keeps moving.

• Keep SVP and EVP-level stakeholders informed and aligned on progress, and give input to business plans and budgets.

• Raise the standard for how Drug Substance Outsourcing works by sharing your approach with category managers and developing sourcing standards.

Who you’ll work with

You will be a senior individual contributor in GSOD Drug Substance Outsourcing, reporting to the Senior Director of the department. The role has no direct reports, but you will lead through influence: category groups and project teams with specialists from MSAT, Supply Chain, Regulatory, Quality, Finance and Legal, as well as colleagues in Global Contract Manufacturing DS, Supply Chain Design, GMS Management and country affiliates.

Externally, you will work with CMOs across the US, Europe and Asia, so you should expect to spend significant time abroad. You will balance partnership and long-term collaboration with the best possible commercial terms for Novo, and you will be at ease handling cross-cultural discussions when tension runs high.

In Global Manufacturing & Supply, colleagues work across the value chain to scale molecules, processes, devices and products for the people who need them. Your primary focus will be Drug Substance, with potential involvement in Drug Product and Devices.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to take decisions independently and to give strategic guidance to senior leaders on the project portfolio. You will build new skills through cross-functional and cross-border work, and you will be recognised for results through clear performance expectations.

You will also have room to challenge convention: to find faster, better ways to run projects and to shape new processes and standards for CMO partnerships.

The pay range for this role is 940,800 – 1,448,700 DKK per year. The final offer reflects your experience and qualifications.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to lead Novo’s most strategic CMO partnerships from strategy to signature, apply for the Project Director role by 19st November 2026 . We review applications on an ongoing basis, so please apply as soon as possible.

For further information, please contact Uffe Holme ufho@novonordisk.com

Health and Safety Supporter

Department: API LP – HSE & Infrastructure

Location: Kalundborg, Denmark

Your impact begins here

As Health and Safety Supporter, you will help create a safe working environment as projects and operations move forward at API LP Kalundborg. You will drive safety improvements, support risk assessments, inspections and incident follow-up, and help ensure that our work complies with Danish legislation, Novo Nordisk requirements and our ISO 45001-aligned management system. Your work will protect colleagues and contractors every day while enabling projects and operations to progress safely.

What you’ll bring

You combine a technical understanding of production with a practical and structured approach to health and safety. You are comfortable working independently while building strong relationships across projects, operations and external partners.

To succeed in this role, you bring:

• 
A technical background, for example as a production or process technician, or a relevant technical academic education.

• 
Professional-level Danish and English, both spoken and written.

• 
Familiarity with management systems such as ISO 45001 and experience of, or familiarity with, project management.

• 
Experience working across functions and the ability to influence stakeholders without formal authority.

• 
Statutory Working Environment training for Health & Safety Representatives and relevant company or health and safety training, such as fire safety, first aid or workplace assessment courses.

• 
A proactive, credible and solution-oriented approach, supported by strong communication skills.

It would be useful, but is not essential, if you have an education within health and safety or two to five years of experience in health and safety management, ideally in an operational or project-based environment.

• Knowledge of Danish health and safety legislation, compliance requirements, risk assessments or accident and incident investigations would also be an advantage.

What you’ll do

As the day-to-day health and safety support for projects and operations at API LP Kalundborg, you will take initiative and help teams continuously improve the way they work safely.

• 
Drive safety improvements throughout project execution and operational readiness, promoting a safety-first and LEAN mindset.

• 
Carry out planned Health, Safety and Environment line walks and safety inspections and provide daily health and safety follow-up, including the processing and follow-up of incidents and near-misses.

• 
Support risk assessments, including assessments involving hazardous media, and contribute to relevant EHS Portal activities.

• 
Support work permits, including GMO-related permits where relevant, as well as Work Wise, emergency response and inspection readiness.

• 
Support the Health & Safety Representative organisation, helping ensure that employee representatives are involved in decisions affecting the working environment.

• 
Support training and introductions and share good health and safety practices across teams and contractors.

Who you’ll work with

You will join API LP – HSE & Infrastructure in Global Manufacturing & Supply and be based at API LP Kalundborg, which will be the scope of your responsibility.

You will collaborate with project managers, people managers in API, Environment, Health and Safety coordinators and colleagues, Health & Safety Partners and Health & Safety Representatives. Externally, you will work with NNE, project subcontractors and consultants.

You will bring these perspectives together, speak up when progress stalls and help teams reach clear, safe decisions at pace.

What you can expect here

You will have a high degree of independence and the trust to use it. You will be supported to perform at your best, encouraged to make your voice heard and given opportunities to contribute your expertise. Working across projects, operations and a broad network of partners will give you opportunities to build new skills and broaden your understanding of the value chain.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 499,600 to 734,400 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position. The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks. Learn more about our Reward Philosophy.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to make safe work the standard across API LP Kalundborg, apply for the Health and Safety Supporter role by 15 November 2026.

Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible via the link.

For questions, please reach out to Martin Winther Wulff, Mww@novonordisk.com.

As Senior Process Engineer, Cleaning, you will keep cleaning processes in API manufacturing stable, validated and continuously improving. You will use data and process science to find root causes, make the case for improvements that matter, and help colleagues grow into subject matter experts. Your work protects product quality in Kalundborg, so more people living with serious chronic diseases can rely on their treatment every day.

What you’ll bring

You are systematic, curious about the science behind a clean process and comfortable taking ownership. You bring:

• A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a relevant scientific or technical discipline.

• 6+ years of experience within cleaning in pharmaceutical or API manufacturing.

• The ability to independently understand the scientific principles behind cleaning, including how chemistry and equipment interact.

• Experience working independently with cleaning validation and process optimisation.

• Strong GMP knowledge and good documentation practice according to cGMP.

• The ability to monitor data, extract insight from it and recommend actionable alternatives, with an appetite for analytical methods.

• The ability to explain complex information to different audiences and bring people on board.

• A quality mindset, respectful teamwork and the independence to make sound decisions.

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience with equipment qualification and process validation (IQ, OQ, PV).

• Experience coaching colleagues or contributing to inspections.

What you’ll do

You will be a driving force for cleaning process understanding in your area, turning data and experience into stable, compliant and continuously improved processes.

• Support daily process execution and troubleshooting, using systematic problem solving to find root causes and drive continuous improvement.

• Use data to visualise, analyse and explain process performance, and drive standardisation of tasks, data collection and analysis.

• Build scientific understanding of the process, linking it to product quality and recommending optimisation projects, with a clear justification for each.

• Develop and perform process confirmation, and grow your responsibility for cleaning validation and other types of process qualification and validation.

• Develop colleagues with more than two years’ experience into subject matter experts, keeping an ongoing dialogue on their individual development plans.

• Keep your area inspection-ready, take part in inspections and share best practice with colleagues across API.

Who you’ll work with

In Global Manufacturing & Supply, colleagues work across the value chain to scale molecules, processes and products for the people who need them. You will join API IO M3 Process Support in Kalundborg, Denmark, reporting to [insert hiring manager name and title].

Every day you will work closely with colleagues in your own department, including Associate Managers, Quality Coordinators, administrative employees and team members. You will also collaborate with other departments across the area to secure good collaboration, systematic problem solving and timely product delivery.

You will share knowledge across API manufacturing facilities, forums and process groups, and communicate results to managers and department managers, and at times to senior leaders within API. Together, you will keep priorities clear and move forward with urgency.

What you can expect here

You will have a high degree of independence within your area, and we expect you to challenge current practices and take initiative. You will be trusted to make your voice heard and to deliver your best work.

The role is built for growth. You will deepen your expertise in cleaning validation and process qualification, strengthen your stakeholder management skills across departments, and learn from colleagues across API facilities while helping others develop.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 651,600 to 956,900 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks. Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to turn process data into stable, compliant cleaning and help colleagues grow into experts, apply for the Senior Process Engineer, Cleaning role by 15 November 2026. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

jobs.occupation: Manager - Software Engineering and Developer Tooling
jobs.description:
Denmark

Smørum

We are looking for a people leader for a mature, well-functioning team of 11 software engineers, split roughly equally between Smørum and Warsaw. You will help colleagues build confidence, use their strengths and grow in their careers through trust and honest feedback. You will be based in Smørum and travel to Warsaw up to six times a year.

The role

The team, called Toolbox, owns Gearbox, an essential tool for building, testing and producing our hearing aid products. Gearbox gives departments a common language and shared data abstractions, and it supports all the communication interfaces needed in development and production. It is data driven and works across product generations, programs and chipsets. Our users rely on Gearbox as a stable, validated tool that performs correctly and gives clear feedback on errors and completed requests.

Your main responsibility is the people in the team. You get to know each person, understand what motivates them and what helps them grow, and you coach rather than direct. Together with the Product Owner and the Scrum Master, you form the team's leadership team and share responsibility for its performance and wellbeing. The Product Owner sets direction and priorities, the Scrum Master supports how the team works, and you lead the people side.

Your main responsibilities

• Lead and develop 11 colleagues by coaching them, giving them ownership and helping them grow in a direction that fits both them and the team.

• Hold regular one-to-ones with each person about expectations, feedback, wellbeing and career development.

• Build the capabilities the team needs today and in the future through development, learning and recruitment, in line with product priorities and the technology strategy.

• Notice early when someone is struggling or losing motivation, and step in with support.

• Handle recruitment, compensation, budget and people processes together with your manager and People & Culture.

• Work as one leadership team with the Product Owner and Scrum Master on team health, learning and delivery.

• Understand the team's technical work and developer workflows well enough to remove obstacles for the team.

What you bring

You may already be a people leader, or you may be ready for your first line manager role. What matters most is the following:

• People first: You are motivated by helping others succeed and grow, and you give people trust and room to take ownership.

• Trust and feedback: You listen, build trust and give clear, honest feedback.

• Difficult conversations: You handle difficult conversations, including about performance, with fairness and respect.

• Leadership experience: You have led or developed others, for example as a manager, tech lead, Scrum Master or mentor.

• Technical understanding: You understand software engineering well enough to engage credibly with developers and architects, typically with a degree in engineering or computer science.

• Leading across sites: You can lead a team split between two locations and keep it working as one team.

Success in the role

After 12 to 18 months, you have earned a high level of trust from every member of the team, and you work closely with the Product Owner and the Scrum Master as one leadership team. Every team member has regular one-to-ones with you and a development plan they own and use. The team's engagement results are stable or improving, the team has kept its key people, and open positions are filled with the skills the team needs. Together with the Product Owner, you have an agreed plan for the skills the team needs over the next two years and how to build them. Colleagues in Smørum and Warsaw experience the same leadership and the same opportunities.

Development in the role: Over time, the role can grow into broader leadership, for example driving developer experience across the organisation or taking on a larger area as a senior manager.

Practical details

Workplace: Kongebakken, Smørum, Denmark (Global HQ)

Team: 11 people across Smørum and Warsaw

Travel: Warsaw up to six times per year

Application deadline: 27.11.26.

Hiring manager Jonas Funk Pedersen can be reached by email: jnfp@demant.com.

Interested?

If you are driven by helping people succeed and grow, and by improving the environment in which software is built, we would like to hear from you.

We screen and invite candidates on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

Demant is a world-leading hearing healthcare and technology group built on a heritage of care, health, and innovation since 1904. jobs.occupation: Advanced Product Development Engineer, Primary Packaging (12-month contact)
jobs.description:
Your impact begins here

As Advanced Product Development Engineer within Primary Packaging, you will shape the primary packaging for Novo's next generation of pre-filled syringes. You will take ownership of technical areas, from new packaging systems to marketed products, working side by side with colleagues across drug and device development, production and supply chain. Your work helps treatments reach people living with serious chronic diseases safely and reliably.

What you’ll bring

You bring hands-on technical experience and enjoy turning design challenges into packaging that works in real life.

• An MSc or BSc in Engineering, Physics, Chemistry or another relevant natural science or technical field.

• Extensive experience in primary packaging for pharmaceutical products, or in medical device or combination product development. Technical depth and fit for the work matter most.

• Experience with requirements and specifications, verification, traceability and risk management in a regulated medical device or pharma environment (GMP/GxP/ISO).

• The ability to independently own a technical area, from assessment and decision to documentation and implementation in the product team and stakeholder landscape.

• Good stakeholder management skills.

• Fluent written and spoken English.

• A creative mindset, pride in delivering on your milestones, and energy for working across functions in a dynamic environment.

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience with pre-filled syringes, syringes, cartridges, vials, stoppers or container closure systems, including Container Closure Integrity.

• Knowledge of how drugs and packaging materials interact, such as coatings, plastics, glues, silicone oil, and chemical and physical drug stability.

• Experience with ISO 15378, ISO 13485 and/or ISO 14971, or with systems engineering.

• Lifecycle management experience, including system ownership for marketed or late-stage products.

• Ability to provide technical direction, bring colleagues and stakeholders together, and drive technical activities towards successful delivery.

• Hands-on experience with technical drawings, tolerances and technical evaluation.

What you’ll do

You will help the team take on a wider portfolio of device projects, including new and larger pre-filled syringe formats and the lifecycle management of existing products.

• Develop primary packaging systems for parenteral administration, such as syringes and vials, from ideation to drug product launch.

• Bring in new primary packaging solutions, including ones not previously used at Novo, or insource existing solutions from external suppliers.

• Document design requirements, safety risk management, mitigations and testing, so that Clinical Trial Applications can be submitted.

• Ensure the right design, material, technical performance, processability and supply chain for each packaging system.

• Support marketed products through system ownership and late-stage changes.

• Scout the market, meet suppliers, and coordinate your own workstream with stakeholders to deliver on time.

Who you’ll work with

jobs.description:
Product Manager, Collective training – SitaWare Aspire

Ready to turn customer insight and new market opportunities into the next chapter of digital defence training? As Product Manager for SitaWare Aspire Collective training, you will lead the strategy and commercial direction for collective training and work closely with the Product Manager for individual training to shape the shared Aspire roadmap.

The job: Lead collective training. Shape SitaWare Aspire together.

You will lead the development and execution of the product strategy for SitaWare Aspire Collective training, defining its future direction, roadmap and commercial success. You will develop the strategy in close collaboration with the Vice President, and innovation will be driven by customer needs and the opportunities AI brings. The Product Manager for individual training holds the same responsibility for the individual training area. Together, collective and individual training form the SitaWare Aspire product, making a strong, interdependent partnership between the two Product Managers essential. You will jointly agree priorities and define the shared Aspire roadmap, ensuring that decisions in each area support the direction and success of the overall product.

In short, you can look forward to:

• identifying and analysing new market opportunities, building the business case and defining the strategy to realise them

• leading concept development for collective training and jointly agreeing priorities and the shared SitaWare Aspire roadmap with the Product Manager responsible for individual training, using business performance and market trends to adjust strategy and tactics together

• defining market requirements through research and dialogue with customers, Sales and domain experts, and working with Defence Product Management, UX designers and architects to develop innovative solutions

• supporting Defence Sales and Defence Services with proposals, product guidance and key customer engagements

• training Sales and Services colleagues at each product release

Your team: Bringing training closer to real operations

You will join Defence Service Development, a committed team of 40+ professionals across Aarhus and Copenhagen. The team develops SitaWare Aspire, a digital platform that brings realistic, hands-on training to users of the SitaWare suite – our command-and-control software for defence environments. Aspire integrates the actual SitaWare application, so users practise in the same interface they use in real operations. Its collective and individual training areas share cloud hosting and pricing, providing a common foundation for the product.

What you bring: Commercial insight that drives product success

You know what it takes to turn a software product’s potential into measurable success. With some years of experience in product management, you bring concrete examples of the impact you have made - and the curiosity to explore what comes next.

To succeed in this role, you bring:

• a master’s degree in software engineering, business development or a related field connecting technology and business

• experience across the product lifecycle - from market and competitor analysis, product discovery, strategy and planning to business cases, pricing and product launches

• a genuine interest in AI, with the curiosity to explore opportunities and the analytical mindset to assess them

• fluent English and excellent communication and collaboration skills that help you build strong partnerships

• excellent stakeholder management skills and an outgoing, enterprising approach to engaging others and moving ideas forward

• a focus on results, strong decision-making skills and the ability to navigate regulations and processes effectively

You will also have opportunities to meet customers, partners and end-users and attend trade shows. The role involves some business travel - around three weeks last year.

Please note that you must be able to present a clean criminal record and have lived in a NATO and/or an EU country for the past seven years as we work with security-classified projects. Read more here.

Welcome to Systematic Aarhus

At our Aarhus office, you can look forward to joining our Employees Club, which offers nearly 100 events a year of both social and professional character. Here, you can take advantage of a range of on-site perks from physiotherapist-led massages and an in-house hairdresser to sports clubs, game tables and even our own padel court. Our canteen is a standout feature, serving a daily selection of delicious and healthy dishes. Beyond the office, you will also enjoy benefits like free ARoS +1 access and various shopping discounts.

Never stop developing

Systematic is uniquely people-centric, truly international and proudly rooted in Denmark with more than 1300 employees. Together, we write intelligent and innovative code to drive progress and improve lives. We develop IT solutions that make a real difference where it matters most. This is why we never stop developing. Here, there is room to be professional and personal. It is not just a place to work but a place to belong.

Start your development here

jobs.occupation: Project Director - Energy Infrastructure, Energy Security & Critical Infrastructure
jobs.description:
Do you want to lead infrastructure projects that power and protect Europe’s future? Do you have the experience, leadership skills and commercial mindset needed to deliver some of Europe’s most strategic energy infrastructure projects? And can you lead multidisciplinary teams? Then, come join COWI!   Create the solutions that will enable a better tomorrow

At COWI, we help our clients address some of society’s most important challenges.

The energy landscape is changing rapidly. Europe is investing in resilient energy infrastructure, decarbonisation, critical infrastructure and strategic energy systems that strengthen security of supply and societal resilience.

To support this development, we are looking for an experienced Project Director to join our Green Energy infrastructure team in Lyngby.

You will become part of our engineering environment working with:

• Hydrogen infrastructure

• CO₂ transportation and storage

• Gas transmission systems

• LNG and ammonia terminals

• Energy storage facilities

• Critical infrastructure

• Defence-related energy infrastructure

• NATO Pipeline System (NPS) developments

• Energy Security & Resilience

You should bring a strong technical foundation and solid experience within one or more of the above, however we are not looking for an expert in all the areas. But we need you to understand complex engineering challenges and provide qualified technical sparring across multidisciplinary teams.

Drive projects from strategy to implementation

A significant part of our project portfolio originates in the early project phases, where clients define future investments and establish the technical and commercial foundations for large infrastructure projects.

As Project Director, you will play a key role in guiding clients through feasibility assessments, concept development, Pre-FEED and FEED phases, before supporting implementation through detailed design and Owner’s Engineer assignments.

You will be responsible for leading multidisciplinary teams across Denmark and our international delivery centres while ensuring technical quality, commercial performance and strong client relationships.

Your key responsibilities

• Lead large and complex multidisciplinary energy infrastructure projects.

• Act as Project Director on feasibility studies, Pre-FEED, FEED, detailed design and Owner’s Engineer assignments.

• Support clients in defining and developing future energy infrastructure investments.

• Develop trusted long-term relationships with clients and key stakeholders.

• Drive commercial performance, governance and project risk management.

• Lead international and multidisciplinary project teams.

• Support business development and major proposal activities.

• Mentor and develop project managers and technical specialists.

• Contribute to COWI’s growth within Energy Security, Resilience and Critical Infrastructure.

• Support emerging opportunities within defence-related energy infrastructure and NATO Pipeline System projects.

   Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

We are looking for a highly experienced project leader who combines solid technical understanding with strong project execution capabilities.

On top of that, you will have:

• 15+ years of experience from multidisciplinary engineering and project management.

• A strong technical background and in-depth experience within one or more areas such as pipelines systems, terminals, process facilities or other energy infrastructure.

• The technical understanding needed to engage with specialists, challenge technical solutions and lead multidisciplinary engineering teams.

• Experience from feasibility studies, Pre-FEED, FEED, detailed design and/or Owner’s Engineer assignments.

• Strong commercial understanding and contract management experience.

• Experience managing large projects and multidisciplinary teams.

• Strong stakeholder management and client engagement skills.

• Experience working in international project environments.

• A relevant engineering degree.

   A place to work and so much more

At COWI, we work together with our customers to shape a sustainable and liveable world. We do it by applying our knowledge and curiosity – and sometimes even our courage – to create the solutions the world needs today to enable a better tomorrow. We support our customers’ transition towards increased sustainability. We strive to lead by example by embedding environmental management, social responsibility and good governance into our business practices and the options we provide to our customers.

We value differences and development and cultivate an environment of belonging and having fun. Because that is what brings out the best in you, at work and at home.

With offices primarily located in the Nordic region, the UK, North America and India, we are currently more than 7,500 people who bring their expertise in engineering, architecture, energy and environment into play.

   Got more questions?

If you have any unanswered questions about the role or what we have to offer, please reach out to Peter Malmkjær, Head of Projects, Green Energy Pipelines at PRMR@COWI.COM.

Get to know us even better at our website, www.cowi.com, where you can learn more about our projects, our strategy, what we want to achieve and what life is like at COWI.

All you need to include in your application is your CV – no photo or application letter. At an interview, you can tell us everything we need to know about why you’re interested in joining COWI. As for the photo, we prefer to form our first impression in person rather than from a picture.

This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.

You will be responsible for ensuring equipment performance, reliability, safety, and long-term value across a global fleet.

Working at the intersection of engineering, operations, project execution, suppliers, and management, you will play a key role in aligning diverse stakeholder needs and translating them into clear requirements, priorities, and improvement initiatives. Success in this role requires strong stakeholder management capabilities, sound technical judgement, and the ability to balance operational, commercial, and safety considerations.

You will drive the development of the traverse equipment roadmap, monitor fleet performance, and lead continuous improvement efforts throughout the equipment lifecycle. By fostering collaboration, standardization, and the adoption of new technologies, you will help ensure that our traverse solutions continue to support safe and efficient offshore operations worldwide.

How You’ll Make an Impact

• Own the traverse equipment lifecycle, ensuring optimal performance, reliability, safety, and long-term business value.

• Translate operational and stakeholder needs into clear requirements, success criteria, and approved improvement initiatives.

• Develop and maintain the traverse equipment roadmap and prioritized backlog, including technology development and investment needs.

• Monitor fleet performance, assess incidents and lessons learned, and drive corrective actions, upgrades, and risk mitigation measures.

• Promote knowledge sharing, technical excellence, and the adoption of innovative technologies across the Equipment organization.

What You Bring

• An Engineering degree (Mechanical, Marine, Civil, Industrial, or similar) and at least 10 years of technical experience in equipment development, maintenance, or asset management within offshore wind or a comparable heavy-industry environment.

• Proven experience with traverse systems, lifting equipment, stabilization systems, motion control technologies, or other equipment used for offshore heavy-load handling.

• Demonstrated experience in equipment ownership, technical leadership, or lifecycle management of complex engineered products.

• Ability to convert operational challenges and user feedback into technical requirements, validation criteria, and improvement plans.

• Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with a structured, proactive, and solution-oriented approach.

About the Team

You will join a global team responsible for the development, maintenance, and continuous improvement of specialized offshore equipment. The team combines operational experience with engineering expertise to ensure equipment reliability, safety, and efficiency throughout its lifecycle. Together, we drive innovation, standardization, and best practices that support offshore wind projects worldwide.

Create the solutions that will enable a better tomorrow

To strengthen our delivery of electrical design services for high-voltage substations, we are looking for an Electrical Designer specialising in substation secondary systems.

You will contribute to new substations, extensions to existing substations, and refurbishment and replacement projects. Your focus will be on preparing detailed electrical designs and documentation for substation control and monitoring systems, including interfaces with protection equipment and auxiliary power supplies.

Your key responsibilities will be to:

• Review electrical drawings for technical accuracy, consistency and compliance with project requirements.

• Coordinate electrical interfaces between primary equipment, control and protection systems, and auxiliary power supplies.

• Provide electrical design support throughout the delivery of high-voltage substation projects.

Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

• A degree in electrical engineering or an equivalent technical qualification.

• Practical experience in electrical design and the preparation of electrical schematics and wiring diagrams.

• Experience using PCSCHEMATIC and SEE Electrical.

• A sound understanding of high-voltage substations, AC and DC auxiliary power supplies, control and monitoring circuits, and protection equipment.

• An understanding of the interfaces between primary equipment and secondary systems.

• A high level of proficiency in both Danish and English, spoken and written.
